000336 | #### 5. Bypass Patterns `[grep-detectable]` (5a P0, 5b P1)
000337 | 
000338 | Two sub-patterns that suppress what the framework would normally catch — making tests pass when they should fail. Listed under P0 because 5a is a silent-pass bug; 5b is a P1 actionability issue documented in the same section for proximity.
000339 | 
000340 | **5a. Conditional assertion bypass** — a load-bearing assertion for the
000341 | scenario's promised outcome is gated behind a runtime condition. If the branch
000342 | is false, that outcome is never verified and no independent unconditional
000343 | meaningful postcondition or failure-producing action can fail the test.
000344 | 
000345 | ```typescript
000346 | // BAD — if spinner never appears, assertion never runs
000347 | if (await spinner.isVisible()) {
000348 |   await expect(spinner).toBeHidden({ timeout: 5000 });
000349 | }
000350 | ```
000351 | 
000352 | **Rule:** Flag P0 only when the conditional assertion is load-bearing for the
000353 | title/action's promised outcome and the false branch has no independent
000354 | unconditional meaningful postcondition or failure-producing action. Do not flag
000355 | a conditional diagnostic or optional-state assertion when the scenario still
000356 | has an unconditional assertion or action that meaningfully proves or enforces
000357 | the promised outcome. Move environment- or feature-flag gates for a required
000358 | outcome to `beforeEach` / declaration-level `test.skip()` so unsupported runs
000359 | are skipped explicitly rather than passing silently.
000360 | 
000361 | **5b. Force true bypass** — `{ force: true }` skips actionability checks (visibility, enabled state, pointer-events), hiding real UX problems that real users would encounter.
000362 | 
000363 | **Rule:** Each `{ force: true }` (including quoted keys and whitespace before
000364 | the colon) on a Playwright/Cypress action must have `// JUSTIFIED:` on the line
000365 | above explaining why the element is not normally actionable. Unrelated APIs such as `fs.rm(..., { force: true })` or `apiClient.request({ force: true })` are not findings. Without a comment, flag P1 and anchor the finding at the line containing the action option.

000367 | #### 7. Focused Test Leak (`test.only` / `it.only`) `[grep-detectable]`
000368 | 
000369 | **Symptom:** A `.only` modifier left in committed code. Test focus applies to
000370 | the invoked project/run, so tests in other files can be silently excluded even
000371 | when the focused file contains only one test.
000372 | 
000373 | ```typescript
000374 | // CRITICAL SILENT-SKIP — file has multiple tests; the others never run
000375 | test.only('should show user profile', async ({ page }) => { ... });
000376 | test('should show settings', ...);   // ← never runs in CI
000377 | 
000378 | // STILL CRITICAL — other files in the invoked project can be excluded
000379 | test.only('the only test in this file', ...);
000380 | ```
000381 | 
000382 | **Rule** (Playwright & Cypress best practices): `.only` is a development-time
000383 | focus tool. It must never be committed. Search `.spec.*/.test.*/.cy.*` for
000384 | direct and optional-call focus modifiers, then trace immutable one-hop aliases:
000385 | `const focused = test.only`, `const focused = test.only.bind(test)`, and
000386 | `const { only } = test` / `const { only: focused } = test`. Report the alias
000387 | call (for example, `focused(...)`) as P0. Accept Playwright-proven receivers and
000388 | Cypress `it` / `test` / `describe` globals only in Cypress-proven spec context.
000389 | For Playwright, follow the exact named, default, CommonJS, or namespace `test`
000390 | binding through relative re-exports. A barrel that exports Playwright `test`
000391 | beside an unrelated `scenario` does not make `scenario.only()` a finding.
000392 | Reject aliases that are reassigned, shadowed, imported from a foreign test
000393 | framework, bound to a different receiver, or derived from an unrelated
000394 | application method named `only`.
000395 | 
000396 | **Fix:** Delete the `.only` modifier. If the test is intentionally isolated,
000397 | use `test.skip()` with a reason on the others, or run a single file via the CLI
000398 | (`--grep` / `--spec`). Audit CI history for skipped runs.
000399 | 
000400 | No `// JUSTIFIED:` exemption exists for either tier — there are no legitimate committed uses.

000402 | #### 8. Missing Assertion `[grep + LLM confirmation]`
000403 | 
000404 | Two candidate sub-patterns where a discarded expression may be standing in for
000405 | the scenario's only verification. The standalone expression is always dead
000406 | code, but it is P0 #8 only when the test otherwise has no independent
000407 | meaningful postcondition or failure-producing action for the promised behavior.

000409 | **8a. Dangling locator** `[Playwright only, grep-detectable]` — a Playwright locator created as a standalone statement, not assigned to a variable, not passed to `expect()`, and not chained with an action. The statement is a complete no-op.
000410 | 
000411 | ```typescript
000412 | // BAD — locator created and immediately discarded
000413 | await page.locator('.selector');
000414 | page.getByRole('button'); // also bad — not even awaited
000415 | ```
000416 | 
000417 | **8b. Boolean result discarded** — `isVisible()` / `isEnabled()` / `isChecked()` / `isDisabled()` / `isEditable()` awaited as a standalone statement. The boolean resolves and is thrown away.
000418 | 
000419 | ```typescript
000420 | // BAD — boolean computed but never checked; asserts nothing
000421 | await el.isVisible();
000422 | await el.isEnabled();
000423 | await page.isVisible('[data-testid="foo"]'); // page-level shorthand with a selector arg — same discard
000424 | ```
000425 | 
000426 | **Rule:** Every Playwright locator expression and every Playwright boolean
000427 | state call must either feed into `expect()`, be assigned and used later, or be
000428 | chained with an action. Standalone Playwright expressions are dead code, but
000429 | report P0 #8 only when the discarded expression is the scenario's intended
000430 | verification and removing it leaves no independent meaningful verification or
000431 | failure evidence. Skip a leftover read in a test that already has real
000432 | assertions. Also skip a discarded pre-check immediately followed by an action
000433 | on the same locator: the action can fail on absence/actionability, while a
000434 | missing outcome assertion is #2 anchored at the action. Do not generalize this
000435 | rule to Cypress: `cy.get(...)` is a retrying query that requires the element to
000436 | exist even without a `.should(...)` chain.

000438 | **Fix:** Replace with web-first assertion — `await expect(locator).toBeVisible()` / `toBeEnabled()` etc. These also auto-retry. Or delete the line if it's leftover debug code.

000445 | `await el.isVisible().catch(() => false)` (covered by `#3` error-swallow),

000451 | **Symptom:** A spec navigates to a protected route without auth, and the resulting login or other wrong surface still satisfies the test's actual assertions.

000453 | **Why it matters:** The test passes against the wrong page and silently reports feature coverage it never exercised.

000455 | **Rule:** First prove the route is protected. Then determine whether the login/wrong surface can satisfy the test's actual assertions. If the wrong surface makes the assertion fail, missing auth is a setup problem rather than a silent always-pass defect: do not report #12 as P0.

000457 | **Config read is mandatory, not optional (severity-stability rule).** Path (b) is invisible from the spec file: a `setup` / `global.setup` project plus a project-level `storageState` in `playwright.config.*` authenticates every spec in that project with nothing in the spec itself. Cypress equivalents are `cy.session()` in a support file and `cypress.config.*` `setupNodeEvents` login tasks. **Open the config and read the `projects` array before deciding severity.** Reviewers who skip this step flag every protected-route spec P0 while reviewers who read it flag none — the same suite then scores 0, 1, or 2 Real P0s across runs, which breaks the counting contract. 000465 | #### 15. Missing `await` on `expect()` `[grep-detectable]`
000466 | 
000467 | **Symptom:** An async Playwright Locator/Page web-first matcher or retry
000468 | assertion (`expect.poll(...).toX()`, `expect(fn).toPass()`) is called without
000469 | observing its Promise.
000470 | 
000471 | ```typescript
000472 | // BAD — matcher starts, but later work is not sequenced after it
000473 | expect(page.locator('.toast')).toBeVisible();
000474 | 
000475 | // BAD — await is on the Locator (a no-op), not on the async matcher
000476 | expect(await page.getByTestId('toast')).toBeVisible();
000477 | 
000478 | // GOOD
000479 | await expect(page.locator('.toast')).toBeVisible();

000482 | **Why it matters:** The matcher runs outside the test's intended sequence. Under Playwright 1.62, a rejection normally fails the current test or worker through `unhandledRejection`, often after teardown has started and with degraded attribution. A matcher that resolves can still race later work.
000483 | 
000484 | **Rule:** Report P1 when an async Locator/Page web-first matcher,
000485 | `expect.poll(...).toX()`, or `expect(fn).toPass()` is not `await`ed or returned.

000487 | `expect` binding through its own local declaration/import/re-export lineage;
000488 | the presence of a Playwright `test` export elsewhere in a mixed fixture/barrel

000569 | #### 10. Flaky Test Patterns `[LLM-only + grep]`
000570 | 
000571 | Two sub-patterns that cause tests to fail intermittently in CI or parallel runs.
000572 | 
000573 | **10a. Positional selectors** — locator `nth()`, `first()`, and `last()` without a comment break when DOM order changes. The scanner deliberately emits broad method-name candidates as `[P1?][LLM-TRIAGE]`; Phase 2 must first prove the receiver is a Playwright/Cypress locator. Unrelated methods such as a database query builder's `.first()` are not findings.
000574 | 
000575 | ```typescript
000576 | // BAD — breaks if DOM order changes
000577 | await expect(items.nth(2)).toContainText('expected text');
000578 | ```
000579 | 
000580 | **Rule:** Prefer `data-testid`, role-based, or attribute selectors. If `nth()` is unavoidable, add `// JUSTIFIED:` explaining why.
000581 | 
000582 | **Exemptions (no `// JUSTIFIED:` needed):**
000583 | - **Method-name self-documents intent** — when the enclosing method's name explicitly conveys positional access (e.g., `getParagraphByIndex(index) { return this.paragraphs.nth(index); }`, `nthRowOf(...)`, `firstResult()`). The name documents the intent.
000584 | - **Fallback selector loops** — `.first()` inside `for (const selector of fallbackSelectors) { … this.page.locator(selector).first() … }`. Here `.first()` means "any match for this candidate selector", not "the first of multiple known elements".
000585 | - **Single-result `toHaveCount(1)` adjacent** — `await expect(items).toHaveCount(1); const only = items.first();` (the count assertion documents that exactly one element exists).
000586 | 
000587 | **Selector priority** (best → worst, per [Playwright docs](https://playwright.dev/docs/best-practices#use-locators)): `getByRole` → `getByLabel` → `getByTestId`/`data-cy` → `getByText` → attribute (`[name]`, `[id]`) → class → generic. Class and generic selectors are "Never" — coupled to CSS and DOM structure.
000588 | 
000589 | **10b. Serial test ordering** `[Playwright only]` — `test.describe.serial()` and `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })`, including multiline configuration objects, make tests order-dependent: a single failure cascades to all subsequent tests, and the suite can't be sharded.
000590 | 
000591 | **Rule:** Replace serial suites with self-contained tests using `beforeEach` for shared setup. If sequential flow is genuinely required, use a single test with `test.step()` blocks. If serial is unavoidable, add `// JUSTIFIED:` on the line above `test.describe.serial(`.
000592 | 
000593 | **10c. Unscoped accessible-name substring match** `[grep + LLM]` — a page-scoped Playwright `getByRole` / `getByLabel` / `getByPlaceholder`, or Cypress Testing Library `cy.findByRole` / `cy.findByLabelText` / `cy.findByPlaceholderText`, with a `name` and **no `exact: true`**. Per [Playwright docs](https://playwright.dev/docs/locators#locate-by-role), the `name` option matches the accessible name as a **case-insensitive substring** by default. When the page also renders user- or data-controlled text (note names, search results, list rows, folder titles), that text can contain the same word, so the locator resolves to 2+ elements and Playwright throws a **strict-mode violation** — thrown immediately, no timeout, so it reads as a hard failure or (when the dynamic content only sometimes collides) an intermittent flake.
000594 | 
000595 | ```typescript
000596 | // BAD — 'Job' is a substring of a note named "Nightly Job Report", so this
000597 | //       resolves to the header link AND the note-list link → strict-mode violation
000598 | await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Job' }).click();
000599 | 
000600 | // GOOD — exact accessible name, scoped to the container it lives in
000601 | await page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link', { name: 'Job', exact: true }).click();
000602 | ```
000603 | 
000604 | **Rule:** A `getByRole`/`getByLabel`/`getByPlaceholder` with a `name` should either be **scoped to a container locator** (`page.locator('.header').getByRole(...)`) or use **`exact: true`** — ideally both — whenever the surrounding page can render dynamic text that might contain the name as a substring. This is the official disambiguation guidance for strict-mode collisions.
000605 | 
000606 | **Fix:** Add `exact: true` to the `name` option, and/or chain the accessor off a stable container locator that bounds the search subtree.
000607 | 
000608 | **Exemptions (skip in Phase 2 — no `// JUSTIFIED:` needed):**
000609 | - **Already scoped:** the accessor is chained off a non-`page` locator (`someContainer.getByRole(...)`) — the subtree already bounds the match.
000610 | - **Already exact:** the call includes `exact: true`.
000611 | - **Regex name:** `name: /^Job$/` — an anchored regex is as precise as `exact`.
000612 | - **Static-only surface:** the suite under test renders no user- or data-controlled text that could contain the name (e.g. a fixed marketing page). Judge by whether the app paints dynamic list/entity text, not by the word alone — a distinctive multi-word name like `"Switch to Classic UI"` is low-risk; a short common word (`"Job"`, `"Run"`, `"Save"`, `"New"`) on a page with dynamic content is the real hit.
000613 | 
000614 | **Cypress equivalent:** `cy.findByRole('link', { name: 'Job' })` (cypress-testing-library) has the same substring default — prefer `{ name: 'Job', exact: true }` or scope with `.within()`.
000615 | 
000616 | **10d. Cypress async callback** `[Cypress only]` `[grep + LLM-TRIAGE]` — an `async` test or hook callback that also queues `cy` commands mixes a returned Promise with Cypress's command queue. The bundled scanner recognizes common arrow/function callback starts and confirms `cy.*` in a bounded body window; Phase 2 confirms nested/multi-line callback boundaries. Remove `async`/`await` and keep Cypress work in the command chain; use `cy.then()` for a real Promise boundary. Do not flag a native-Promise-only async callback as this command-queue smell.
000617 | 
000618 | **10e. Assigned Cypress command return** `[Cypress only]` — `const value = cy.get(...)` stores a Chainable, not the yielded DOM/application value. The bundled scanner covers same-line declarations, including TypeScript annotations; Phase 2 checks split declarations. Keep dependent assertions in `.then()`/`.should()` or use an alias. Do not flag ordinary application-value assignment or Cypress's synchronous Sinon utilities `cy.spy()`/`cy.stub()`, which intentionally return the created test double.
000619 | 
000620 | **10f. Unsafe continued Cypress action chain** `[Cypress only]` `[grep + LLM-TRIAGE]` — an action such as `.click()` or `.type()` is followed by another assertion/action in the same chain. The bundled scanner reconstructs bounded same-line and multiline chains; Phase 2 confirms the subject-stability risk. Cypress retries queries and assertions but not the action, so the continued chain can retain a detached/stale subject. End the chain and re-query the intended post-action state. Skip when project evidence proves the subject remains stable and the chain is intentionally atomic.

000717 | ```typescript

000719 | let testNotebookSequence = 0;

000810 | ### P2 — Nice to Fix (maintenance / robustness)
000811 | 
000812 | Weak but not wrong. Address when refactoring or before adopting wider conventions.
000813 | 
000814 | #### 11. YAGNI + Zombie Specs `[LLM-only]`
000815 | 
000816 | Two sub-patterns: unused code in Page Objects, and zombie spec files.
000817 | 
000818 | **11a. YAGNI in Page Objects and Utility Modules** — POM or utility/helper file
000819 | has locators, methods, or exported functions never referenced by any spec or
000820 | other module. A single-use member is only a review candidate: report it when
000821 | inlining clearly removes indirection without duplicating meaningful setup,
000822 | erasing stable domain vocabulary, or violating an established repository
000823 | boundary. Or a POM class extends a parent with zero additional members and no
000824 | documented convention justifies the type boundary.
000825 | 
000826 | **Procedure:**
000827 | 1. List all public members of each changed POM file AND all exported symbols of each changed utility module (`utils.ts`, `helpers.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, etc.)
000828 | 2. Grep each member/export across all test files, POMs, and other utility modules
000829 | 3. Classify: USED / INTERNAL-ONLY (`private` for POMs, non-`export` for utility modules) / UNUSED (delete) / SINGLE-USE (inline at the call site)
000830 | 4. For a single-use symbol, inspect complexity, domain meaning, and repository
000831 |    conventions before deciding whether inlining is an improvement.
000832 | 5. Check if any POM class has zero members beyond what it inherits — empty
000833 |    wrappers add no value unless the convention is intentional.
000834 | 
000835 | **Common patterns:** Convenience wrappers (`clickEdit()` when specs use `editButton.click()`), getter methods (`getCount()` when specs use `toHaveCount()`), state checkers (`isVisible()` when specs assert on locators directly), pre-built "just in case" locators, empty subclass created for future expansion. In utility modules: single-use auth helpers (`isLoginPageVisible()` called by exactly one other utility), single-use REST helpers (`getDefaultInterpreterGroup()` called by exactly one create function), single-use waits (`waitForNotebookParagraphVisible()` invoked from one navigation helper).
000836 | 
000837 | **Single-use Util wrappers** — a separate `*Util` / `*Helper` class OR a
000838 | standalone exported function called from only one place warrants inspection,
000839 | not automatic deletion. Inline only when the wrapper adds no stable domain
000840 | vocabulary, reusable validation, non-trivial setup boundary, or documented
000841 | architectural role.
000842 | 
000843 | **Rule:** Delete unused members and exports. Make internal-only POM members
000844 | `private`; drop the `export` keyword from utility functions used only inside
000845 | their own module. Treat usage count as evidence, not the verdict: recommend
000846 | inlining a single-use helper only when the resulting code is simpler and the
000847 | boundary carries no independent meaning. Flag empty wrapper classes for review
000848 | when no documented convention explains them.
000849 | 
000850 | **11b. Zombie spec files** — An entire spec file whose tests are all subsets of tests in another spec file covering the same feature. The file adds no coverage that isn't already verified elsewhere.
000851 | 
000852 | **Procedure:** After reviewing all files in scope, cross-check spec files with similar names or feature coverage. If every test in file A is a subset of a test in file B, flag file A for deletion.
000853 | 
000854 | **Common patterns:** `feature-basic.spec.ts` where every case also appears in `feature-full.spec.ts`; a 1–2 test file created as a "quick smoke" that was never expanded while a comprehensive suite grew alongside it.
000855 | 
000856 | **Rule:** Delete the zombie file. If any test in it is not covered elsewhere, migrate it to the comprehensive suite first.
000857 | 
000858 | **Output:**
000859 | ```
000860 | | File | Member | Used In | Status |
000861 | |------|--------|---------|--------|
000862 | | modal-page.ts | openModal() | (none) | DELETE |
000863 | | modal-page.ts | closeButton | internal only | PRIVATE |
000864 | | search-page.ts | (class body empty) | — | REVIEW |
000865 | | basic.spec.ts | (entire file) | covered by full.spec.ts | DELETE |
000866 | ```
000867 | 
000868 | #### 21. Manually-Captured Session-File Dependency `[LLM-only]`
000869 | 
000870 | **Symptom:** A spec, fixture, or project config loads a `storageState` JSON (e.g. `auth/member.json`) that only a manual capture script or a developer's one-off login produces — nothing in the automated test setup can regenerate it.
000871 | 
000872 | **Why it matters:** The file is absent on fresh clones and CI, and silently expires. The suite then fails — or worse, soft-skips — for reasons unrelated to the code under test, and nobody trusts the signal.
000873 | 
000874 | **Rule:** Session state must be reproducible from code: an API-login helper or a `setup` project that writes `storageState` before dependent specs run. A committed or manually captured file may serve only as a cache with a programmatic fallback.
000875 | 
000876 | **Detection (LLM):** For each `storageState:` reference (spec, fixture, or `playwright.config` project), trace what writes that path. If only a manual script — or nothing in-repo — produces it, flag.
000877 | 
000878 | #### 23. Fixture Ignores Conditional Render Guards `[LLM-only]`
000879 | 
000880 | **Symptom:** A seeded list/item fixture satisfies the API type but not the *render guards* of the component that displays it — e.g. a "Liked" tab whose item component does `if (tabIsLiked && !item.liked) return null;`, while the fixture seeds `liked: false`. The UI renders an empty container; the test fails with "element not found" that looks like infra flake, or—worse—a negative assertion (`toHaveCount(0)`, empty-state check) passes for the wrong reason.
000881 | 
000882 | **Why it matters:** Type-correct fixtures aren't render-correct fixtures. Components self-hide on field+view-state combinations (`liked` in a liked view, `enabled`, `membershipOnly`, date windows, `items.slice(1)` init drops), and these guards live in the component, not the API contract. Hours go to debugging "flaky" tests whose mock data was simply unrenderable.
000883 | 
000884 | **Rule:** Before seeding a list fixture, read the item component's early returns and filters; seed fields so the item passes every guard for the view under test. Document each discovered guard next to the fixture (e.g. "Like-tab items must seed `liked: true`") so the next generated test doesn't rediscover it.
000885 | 
000886 | **Detection (LLM):** For each fixture consumed by a conditionally-rendered component, open the component and collect conditions that suppress rendering (early `return null`, `.filter()`, `.slice()`, a template guard such as `@if`/`v-if`/`{cond && …}` around the whole subtree). Cross-check the seeded values against them. Flag mismatches, and flag negative assertions whose truth could come from a guard-suppressed render rather than the intended state.
000887 | 
000888 | **Scope note:** the guard need not sit on a list/card item — the same failure appears whenever a *container* is gated on a value the test controls indirectly. A results panel wrapped in `@if (result.type === TABLE)` suppresses every control inside it when the fixture produces a different result type, so a test targeting a toolbar button inside that panel fails with "element not found" and looks like infra flake. When a control the test needs is missing, walk up the template to the nearest guard before suspecting the selector.
000889 |

000001 | # Cross-Framework Verification Rules (V1–V6)
000002 | 
000003 | <!-- V-RULE-CONTRACT: V1=primary-outcome;V2=assertion-falsification;V3=behavior-fault-injection;V4=write-contract-proof;V5=repeat-and-isolation;V6=independent-re-review;verdicts=PASS,FAIL,CANNOT_VERIFY,ERROR;source=immutable;install=forbidden -->
000004 | <!-- V-RESULT-SCHEMA: candidate,runner,verification.V1,verification.V2,verification.V3,verification.V4,verification.V5,verification.V6,sourceUnchanged,temporaryArtifactsRemaining -->
000005 | 
000006 | V-rules are runtime proof recommendations, not new smell IDs. Keep the 24-pattern taxonomy and F1-F15 failure taxonomy stable.
000007 | 
000008 | | ID | Contract | Playwright proof | Cypress proof |
000009 | |---|---|---|---|
000010 | | V1 | One primary observable outcome matches the title/actions | one load-bearing web-first assertion | one load-bearing retryable `.should()`/`expect` assertion |
000011 | | V2 | Safely invert the primary assertion in a temporary copy; expect red | `.toBeVisible()` ↔ `.not.toBeVisible()`, text/URL/count equivalents | `'be.visible'` ↔ `'not.be.visible'`, text/value/length equivalents |
000012 | | V3 | Corrupt an evidenced dependency; unchanged assertion must turn red | `page.route()` or existing fixture | `cy.intercept()` or existing fixture |
000013 | | V4 | Prove write method/endpoint/payload/cardinality and failed-write behavior | `waitForRequest`, route-hit capture | alias/intercept plus `cy.wait()` request inspection |
000014 | | V5 | Pass bounded solo, repeat, suite-context, and supported parallel checks | repository-native Playwright script | repository-native Cypress script/repeat facility |
000015 | | V6 | A writer/debugger cannot approve its own output | rerun e2e-reviewer after repair | rerun e2e-reviewer after repair |
000016 | 
000017 | Verdicts: `PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_VERIFY` with a concrete reason, or verifier `ERROR`. Do not install packages, require `npx`, mutate the trusted source spec, invent an endpoint, or treat a verifier error as a product defect.
000018 | 
000019 | ## Project-rule merge
000020 | 
000021 | Discover `AGENTS.md`, testing docs, package scripts, ESLint config, framework config, CI, fixtures, POMs/custom commands, and existing verifier tooling before reviewing.
000022 | 
000023 | 1. **Equivalent:** emit one finding with both project-rule and e2e-skills provenance.
000024 | 2. **Project stronger:** follow it for generation and report a project-convention issue only at its warranted severity.
000025 | 3. **e2e-skills stronger/semantic:** keep the e2e-skills finding; a green linter cannot prove intent.
000026 | 4. **Conflict:** P0 silent-pass safety wins over style. P1 can be suppressed only by a concrete local rationale; P2/style follows project convention.
000027 | 
000028 | Existing project lint is evidence, not a dependency. The target repository is
000029 | untrusted by default. Static review never treats repository documentation as
000030 | execution approval. Execute target-controlled tooling only when the user has
000031 | both explicitly trusted the checkout and approved the exact command, including
000032 | its environment and flags. The same gate covers documented lint commands,
000033 | package scripts, local binaries, and Tier 1. Without both approvals, record the
000034 | probe as `recommended/unexecuted`; the bundled scanner remains the deterministic
000035 | baseline. Never auto-download ESLint, plugins, AST tools, or mutation tools.
000036 | 
000037 | ## Finding-to-proof map
000038 | 
000039 | | Pattern | Recommended verification |
000040 | |---|---|
000041 | | #1 name/assertion mismatch, #2 missing Then | V1, then V3 when an evidenced dependency exists |
000042 | | #3/#3b error swallowing, #5 conditional assertion, #8 missing assertion, #15/#16 missing await | V2 |
000043 | | #4 vacuous/non-retrying/under-specified assertions, including #4i unproven absence and #4j omitted ARIA names | V2; V3 for selector/data/accessible-name provenance |
000044 | | #9/#10 flaky patterns, #19 mutable state | V5 |
000045 | | #20 unmocked real writes | V3 + V4, without touching production/third-party systems |
000046 | | #22 optimistic UI without call proof | V3 + V4 |
000047 | 
000048 | Runtime proof remains optional in a static review. Recommend only the smallest evidence-backed probe; do not claim it ran unless an actual command and result are available.
000049 | 
000050 | When runtime proof is actually requested, require a structured result containing the candidate path, repository-native runner, explicit V1–V6 verdict objects, evidence or a concrete reason, `sourceUnchanged`, and `temporaryArtifactsRemaining`. Missing applicable V-rules are not implicit passes. Static review output does not fabricate this object when no runtime command ran.

000326 | # Stream external-tool output through byte and line limiters before any output
000327 | # can be materialized in a shell variable. `head` bounds even one hostile
000328 | # unterminated line; awk then stops after limit+1 records. The producer/head may
000329 | # receive SIGPIPE (141) only after a confirmed limiter trip. Any other producer
000330 | # failure remains an infrastructure error owned by the caller.
000331 | capture_bounded_command() {
000332 |   local output_file="$1" error_file="$2" marker_file="$3"
000333 |   shift 3
000334 |   local byte_window=$((E2E_SMELL_MAX_RULE_BYTES + 1))
000335 |   local -a _capture_status=()
000336 |   : > "$output_file"
000337 |   : > "$error_file"
000338 |   : > "$marker_file"
000339 |   "$@" 2>&1 |
000340 |     head -c "$byte_window" |
000341 |     awk -v max_lines="$E2E_SMELL_MAX_RULE_HITS" -v marker="$marker_file" '
000342 |       NR > max_lines {
000343 |         print "lines" > marker
000344 |         exit 42
000345 |       }
000346 |       { print }
000347 |     ' > "$output_file"
000348 |   _capture_status=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")

000355 |   if [[ -s "$marker_file" ]]; then

002826 | # Return only executable source for one hit line. Strings are replaced with

002842 |       out = ""

002845 |         c = substr(s, i, 1)
002846 |         nchar = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
002847 |         if (lex_block) {
002848 |           if (c == "*" && nchar == "/") {
002849 |             lex_block = 0
002850 |             i++
002851 |           }

002853 |         }
002854 |         if (lex_regex) {
002855 |           if (lex_escape) {
002856 |             lex_escape = 0
002857 |           } else if (c == "\\") {
002858 |             lex_escape = 1
002859 |           } else if (c == "[") {
002860 |             regex_class = 1
002861 |           } else if (c == "]") {
002862 |             regex_class = 0

002873 |             lex_escape = 0
002874 |           } else if (c == "\\") {
002875 |             lex_escape = 1
002876 |           } else if (lex_quote == "`" && c == "$" && nchar == "{") {
002877 |             lex_quote = ""
002878 |             template_depth = 1
002879 |             value = ""
002880 |             i++
002881 |           } else if (c == lex_quote) {

002884 |             value = ""

002909 |         }

002911 |           lex_block = 1

002913 |           continue
002914 |         }

000106 | def strict_json_loads(data: bytes | str) -> object:
000107 |     if isinstance(data, bytes):
000108 |         if data.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
000109 |             raise ValueError("JSON BOM is forbidden")

000111 |             text = data.decode("utf-8")

000113 |             raise ValueError(f"invalid JSON UTF-8: {exc}") from exc
000114 |     else:
000115 |         text = data

000117 |         raise ValueError("JSON BOM is forbidden")

000119 |     if start == len(text):
000120 |         raise ValueError("invalid JSON: input is empty")
000121 |     decoder = json.JSONDecoder(
000122 |         object_pairs_hook=reject_duplicate_keys,
000123 |         parse_constant=reject_nonfinite_number,

000125 |     try:

000127 |     except (RecursionError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
000128 |         raise ValueError(f"invalid JSON: {exc}") from exc
000129 |     if text[end:].strip():
000130 |         raise ValueError("invalid JSON: trailing data is forbidden")

000134 | def open_trusted_directory(path: Path, description: str) -> int:
000135 |     """Open an absolute directory from the filesystem root without following links."""

000143 |         for component in absolute.parts[1:]:
000144 |             next_fd = os.open(component, directory_flags, dir_fd=current_fd)
000145 |             os.close(current_fd)

000149 |         if current_fd is not None:

000170 | def read_bounded_file(
000171 |     report_root: Path,
000172 |     artifact: Path,
000173 |     max_bytes: int,
000174 | ) -> bytes:
000175 |     require_secure_descriptor_support()
000176 |     absolute_root = Path(os.path.abspath(report_root))
000177 |     absolute_artifact = Path(os.path.abspath(artifact))
000178 |     try:
000179 |         lexical_relative = absolute_artifact.relative_to(absolute_root)
000180 |     except ValueError as exc:
000181 |         raise ValueError(f"artifact is outside the report root: {artifact}") from exc
000182 |     if not lexical_relative.parts:
000183 |         raise ValueError(f"artifact is not a regular file: {artifact}")
000184 | 
000185 |     close_on_exec = getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0)
000186 |     directory_flags = os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | close_on_exec
000187 |     file_flags = (
000188 |         os.O_RDONLY
000189 |         | os.O_NOFOLLOW
000190 |         | getattr(os, "O_NONBLOCK", 0)
000191 |         | close_on_exec
000192 |     )
000193 |     root_fd = open_trusted_directory(absolute_root, "report root")
000194 |     current_fd = root_fd
000195 |     opened_directory_fds: list[int] = []
000196 |     artifact_fd: int | None = None
000197 |     try:
000198 |         for component in lexical_relative.parts[:-1]:
000199 |             next_fd = os.open(component, directory_flags, dir_fd=current_fd)
000200 |             opened_directory_fds.append(next_fd)
000201 |             current_fd = next_fd
000202 |         artifact_fd = os.open(
000203 |             lexical_relative.parts[-1],
000204 |             file_flags,
000205 |             dir_fd=current_fd,
000206 |         )
000207 |         metadata = os.fstat(artifact_fd)
000208 |         if not stat.S_ISREG(metadata.st_mode):
000209 |             raise ValueError(f"artifact is not a regular file: {artifact}")
000210 |         if metadata.st_size > max_bytes:
000211 |             raise ValueError(
000212 |                 f"artifact exceeds the {max_bytes}-byte limit: {artifact}"
000213 |             )
000214 | 
000215 |         chunks: list[bytes] = []
000216 |         remaining = max_bytes + 1
000217 |         while remaining:
000218 |             chunk = os.read(artifact_fd, min(64 * 1024, remaining))
000219 |             if not chunk:
000220 |                 break
000221 |             chunks.append(chunk)
000222 |             remaining -= len(chunk)
000223 |         data = b"".join(chunks)
000224 |         if len(data) > max_bytes:
000225 |             raise ValueError(
000226 |                 f"artifact exceeds the {max_bytes}-byte limit: {artifact}"
000227 |             )
000228 |         current_metadata = os.fstat(artifact_fd)
000229 |         if (
000230 |             descriptor_fingerprint(current_metadata)
000231 |             != descriptor_fingerprint(metadata)
000232 |             or len(data) != current_metadata.st_size
000233 |         ):
000234 |             raise ValueError(f"artifact changed while being read: {artifact}")
000235 |         return data
000236 |     except OSError as exc:
000237 |         raise ValueError(
000238 |             f"unsafe, symlinked, or unreadable artifact path: {artifact}: {exc}"
000239 |         ) from exc
000240 |     finally:
000241 |         if artifact_fd is not None:
000242 |             os.close(artifact_fd)
000243 |         for directory_fd in reversed(opened_directory_fds):
000244 |             os.close(directory_fd)
000245 |         os.close(root_fd)

000446 | def computed_test_outcome(test: dict[str, object]) -> str:
000447 |     expected_status = test.get("expectedStatus", "passed")
000448 |     if (
000449 |         not isinstance(expected_status, str)
000450 |         or expected_status not in PLAYWRIGHT_RESULT_STATUSES
000451 |     ):
000452 |         raise ValueError(
000453 |             "report JSON schema requires a valid test expectedStatus"
000454 |         )
000455 |     results = test.get("results")
000456 |     assert isinstance(results, list)
000457 |     skipped = 0
000458 |     expected = 0
000459 |     unexpected = 0
000460 |     for result in results:
000461 |         assert isinstance(result, dict)
000462 |         status = result.get("status")
000463 |         if (
000464 |             not isinstance(status, str)
000465 |             or status not in PLAYWRIGHT_RESULT_STATUSES
000466 |         ):
000467 |             raise ValueError(
000468 |                 "report result status contradicts the Playwright JSON schema"
000469 |             )
000470 |         if status == "interrupted":
000471 |             unexpected += 1
000472 |             continue
000473 |         if status == "skipped" and expected_status == "skipped":
000474 |             skipped += 1
000475 |         elif status == "skipped":
000476 |             continue
000477 |         elif status == expected_status:
000478 |             expected += 1
000479 |         else:
000480 |             unexpected += 1
000481 |     if expected == 0 and unexpected == 0:
000482 |         return "skipped"
000483 |     if unexpected == 0:
000484 |         return "expected"
000485 |     if expected == 0 and skipped == 0:
000486 |         return "unexpected"

000490 | def report_specs(report: object) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
000491 |     if not isinstance(report, dict) or not isinstance(report.get("suites"), list):
000492 |         raise ValueError("report JSON schema requires a root suites array")

000494 |     specs: list[dict[str, object]] = []
000495 |     canonical_spec_ids: set[int] = set()
000496 |     suites = report["suites"]
000497 |     suite_stack = list(reversed(suites))
000498 |     while suite_stack:
000499 |         suite = suite_stack.pop()
000500 |         if not isinstance(suite, dict):
000501 |             raise ValueError("report JSON schema requires suite objects")
000502 |         child_suites = suite.get("suites", [])
000503 |         suite_specs = suite.get("specs")
000504 |         if not isinstance(child_suites, list) or not isinstance(suite_specs, list):
000505 |             raise ValueError(
000506 |                 "report JSON schema requires suites/specs arrays on every suite"
000507 |             )
000508 |         suite_stack.extend(reversed(child_suites))

000510 |             if (
000511 |                 not isinstance(spec, dict)
000512 |                 or not isinstance(spec.get("ok"), bool)
000513 |                 or not isinstance(spec.get("tests"), list)
000514 |             ):
000515 |                 raise ValueError(
000516 |                     "report JSON schema requires each spec to have bool ok "
000517 |                     "and tests array"
000518 |                 )
000519 |             canonical_spec_ids.add(id(spec))
000520 |             specs.append(spec)
000521 |             if len(specs) > MAX_OUTPUT_RECORDS:
000522 |                 raise ValueError(
000523 |                     f"report exceeds the {MAX_OUTPUT_RECORDS}-spec limit"
000524 |                 )
000525 |             for test in spec["tests"]:
000526 |                 if (
000527 |                     not isinstance(test, dict)
000528 |                     or not isinstance(test.get("status"), str)
000529 |                     or not isinstance(test.get("results"), list)
000530 |                 ):
000531 |                     raise ValueError(
000532 |                         "report JSON schema requires test status and results array"
000533 |                     )
000534 |                 outcome = test["status"]
000535 |                 if outcome not in PLAYWRIGHT_OUTCOMES:
000536 |                     raise ValueError(
000537 |                         "report JSON schema requires a valid test status"
000538 |                     )
000539 |                 if len(test["results"]) > MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_TEST:
000540 |                     raise ValueError(
000541 |                         f"test exceeds the "
000542 |                         f"{MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_TEST}-attempt limit"
000543 |                     )
000544 |                 for result in test["results"]:
000545 |                     if not isinstance(result, dict):
000546 |                         raise ValueError(
000547 |                             "report JSON schema requires result objects"
000548 |                         )
000549 |                 computed_outcome = computed_test_outcome(test)
000550 |                 if outcome != computed_outcome:
000551 |                     raise ValueError(
000552 |                         f"report test status={outcome} contradicts results "
000553 |                         f"outcome={computed_outcome}"
000554 |                     )
000555 |             expected_ok = all(
000556 |                 test["status"] in {"expected", "flaky", "skipped"}
000557 |                 for test in spec["tests"]
000558 |             )
000559 |             if spec["ok"] != expected_ok:
000560 |                 raise ValueError(
000561 |                     f"report spec.ok={spec['ok']} contradicts test statuses"
000562 |                 )

000564 |     # A spec-shaped object outside suites/specs is ambiguous. Reject it rather
000565 |     # than silently returning an empty/partial failure set.

000568 |         current = stack.pop()

000571 |                 "ok" in current
000572 |                 and "tests" in current
000573 |                 and id(current) not in canonical_spec_ids
000574 |             ):
000575 |                 raise ValueError(
000576 |                     "report JSON schema contains a spec-shaped object outside "
000577 |                     "suites/specs"
000578 |                 )
000579 |             stack.extend(current.values())
000580 |         elif isinstance(current, list):
000581 |             stack.extend(current)

000691 | def safe_zip_infos(archive: zipfile.ZipFile) -> dict[str, zipfile.ZipInfo]:
000692 |     infos = archive.infolist()
000693 |     if len(infos) > MAX_ZIP_ENTRIES:
000694 |         raise ValueError(f"ZIP exceeds the {MAX_ZIP_ENTRIES}-entry limit")
000695 |     by_name: dict[str, zipfile.ZipInfo] = {}
000696 |     total_size = 0
000697 |     for info in infos:
000698 |         if info.filename in by_name:
000699 |             raise ValueError(f"duplicate ZIP entry: {info.filename}")
000700 |         by_name[info.filename] = info
000701 |         path = PurePosixPath(info.filename)
000702 |         if (
000703 |             not info.filename
000704 |             or info.filename.startswith("/")
000705 |             or "\\" in info.filename
000706 |             or ".." in path.parts
000707 |         ):
000708 |             raise ValueError(f"unsafe ZIP entry name: {info.filename}")
000709 |         mode = info.external_attr >> 16
000710 |         file_type = stat.S_IFMT(mode)
000711 |         name_is_directory = info.filename.endswith("/")
000712 |         mode_is_directory = bool(file_type) and stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
000713 |         if file_type and name_is_directory != mode_is_directory:
000714 |             raise ValueError(
000715 |                 "ZIP directory mode/name disagreement: "
000716 |                 f"{info.filename}"
000717 |             )
000718 |         if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
000719 |             raise ValueError(f"symlink ZIP entry is forbidden: {info.filename}")
000720 |         if file_type and not (
000721 |             stat.S_ISREG(mode) or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
000722 |         ):
000723 |             raise ValueError(f"special-file ZIP entry is forbidden: {info.filename}")
000724 |         if info.flag_bits & 0x1:
000725 |             raise ValueError(f"encrypted ZIP entry is forbidden: {info.filename}")
000726 |         if info.compress_type not in ALLOWED_ZIP_METHODS:
000727 |             raise ValueError(
000728 |                 f"unsupported ZIP compression method: {info.filename}"
000729 |             )
000730 |         if info.file_size > MAX_ZIP_ENTRY_BYTES:
000731 |             raise ValueError(
000732 |                 f"ZIP entry exceeds the {MAX_ZIP_ENTRY_BYTES}-byte limit: "
000733 |                 f"{info.filename}"
000734 |             )
000735 |         total_size += info.file_size
000736 |         if total_size > MAX_ZIP_TOTAL_BYTES:
000737 |             raise ValueError(
000738 |                 f"ZIP exceeds the {MAX_ZIP_TOTAL_BYTES}-byte expanded limit"
000739 |             )
000740 |         if info.file_size:
000741 |             if not info.compress_size:
000742 |                 raise ValueError(f"ZIP entry has an invalid compression ratio: {info.filename}")
000743 |             ratio = info.file_size / info.compress_size
000744 |             if ratio > MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO:
000745 |                 raise ValueError(
000746 |                     f"ZIP entry exceeds the {MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO}:1 "
000747 |                     f"compression ratio: {info.filename}"
000748 |                 )
000749 |     return by_name

000809 | def project_trace_record(record: object, entry: str) -> dict[str, object] | None:
000810 |     if not isinstance(record, dict):
000811 |         return None
000812 |     if entry.endswith("trace.network"):
000813 |         if record.get("type") != "resource-snapshot":
000814 |             return None
000815 |         snapshot = record.get("snapshot")
000816 |         if not isinstance(snapshot, dict):
000817 |             return None
000818 |         request = snapshot.get("request")
000819 |         response = snapshot.get("response")
000820 |         request = request if isinstance(request, dict) else {}
000821 |         response = response if isinstance(response, dict) else {}
000822 |         status = response.get("status")
000823 |         failure = (
000824 |             snapshot.get("_failureText")
000825 |             or response.get("errorText")
000826 |             or request.get("failure")
000827 |         )
000828 |         if isinstance(failure, dict):
000829 |             failure = failure.get("errorText") or failure.get("message")
000830 |         failure_text = trace_string(failure)
000831 |         if not (
000832 |             isinstance(status, (int, float))
000833 |             and not isinstance(status, bool)
000834 |             and status >= 400
000835 |         ) and not failure_text:
000836 |             return None
000837 |         return redact_sensitive(
000838 |             {
000839 |                 "kind": "network-error",
000840 |                 "method": trace_string(request.get("method")),
000841 |                 "url": trace_string(request.get("url") or snapshot.get("url")),
000842 |                 "status": (
000843 |                     status
000844 |                     if isinstance(status, (int, float))
000845 |                     and not isinstance(status, bool)
000846 |                     else None
000847 |                 ),
000848 |                 "statusText": trace_string(response.get("statusText")),
000849 |                 "failure": failure_text,
000850 |             }
000851 |         )
000852 | 
000853 |     record_type = record.get("type")
000854 |     if record_type == "after" and record.get("error") is not None:
000855 |         return redact_sensitive(
000856 |             {
000857 |                 "kind": "failed-action",
000858 |                 "apiName": trace_string(record.get("apiName")),
000859 |                 "callId": trace_string(record.get("callId")),
000860 |                 "error": projected_error(record.get("error")),
000861 |             }
000862 |         )
000863 |     if (
000864 |         record_type == "console"
000865 |         and str(record.get("messageType", "")).lower() == "error"
000866 |     ):
000867 |         return redact_sensitive(
000868 |             {
000869 |                 "kind": "console-error",
000870 |                 "text": trace_string(record.get("text")),
000871 |                 "location": projected_trace_location(record.get("location")),
000872 |             }
000873 |         )
000874 |     method = str(record.get("method", "")).lower().replace("-", "")
000875 |     normalized_type = str(record_type or "").lower().replace("-", "")
000876 |     if method == "pageerror" or normalized_type == "pageerror":
000877 |         params = record.get("params")
000878 |         params = params if isinstance(params, dict) else {}
000879 |         error = (
000880 |             params.get("error")
000881 |             or record.get("error")
000882 |             or params.get("message")
000883 |             or record.get("message")
000884 |         )
000885 |         return redact_sensitive(
000886 |             {
000887 |                 "kind": "page-error",
000888 |                 "error": projected_error(error),
000889 |             }

000894 | def read_trace_entry(data: bytes, entry: str) -> list[object]:
000895 |     if not EXPECTED_TRACE_ENTRY.fullmatch(entry):
000896 |         raise ValueError(
000897 |             "entry is not an expected trace entry "
000898 |             "(trace.trace, trace.network, or a numeric-prefixed equivalent)"
000899 |         )
000900 |     archive, infos = open_trace_archive(data)
000901 |     try:
000902 |         with archive:
000903 |             info = infos.get(entry)
000904 |             if info is None:
000905 |                 raise ValueError(f"expected trace entry is absent: {entry}")
000906 |             mode = info.external_attr >> 16
000907 |             file_type = stat.S_IFMT(mode)
000908 |             if (
000909 |                 info.is_dir()
000910 |                 or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
000911 |                 or (file_type and not stat.S_ISREG(mode))
000912 |             ):
000913 |                 raise ValueError(
000914 |                     f"selected trace entry is not a regular file: {entry}"
000915 |                 )
000916 |             if info.file_size > MAX_SELECTED_ENTRY_BYTES:
000917 |                 raise ValueError(
000918 |                     f"selected entry exceeds the "
000919 |                     f"{MAX_SELECTED_ENTRY_BYTES}-byte limit: {entry}"
000920 |                 )
000921 |             records: list[object] = []
000922 |             projected_bytes = 2
000923 |             selected_bytes = 0
000924 |             with archive.open(info, "r") as source:
000925 |                 line_number = 0
000926 |                 while True:
000927 |                     line = source.readline(MAX_NDJSON_LINE_BYTES + 2)
000928 |                     if not line:
000929 |                         break
000930 |                     line_number += 1
000931 |                     selected_bytes += len(line)
000932 |                     if selected_bytes > MAX_SELECTED_ENTRY_BYTES:
000933 |                         raise ValueError(
000934 |                             f"selected entry exceeds the "
000935 |                             f"{MAX_SELECTED_ENTRY_BYTES}-byte limit: {entry}"
000936 |                         )
000937 |                     if len(line.rstrip(b"\r\n")) > MAX_NDJSON_LINE_BYTES:
000938 |                         raise ValueError(
000939 |                             f"trace line {line_number} exceeds the "
000940 |                             f"{MAX_NDJSON_LINE_BYTES}-byte limit"
000941 |                         )
000942 |                     if not line.strip():
000943 |                         continue
000944 |                     try:
000945 |                         record = strict_json_loads(line)
000946 |                     except ValueError as exc:
000947 |                         raise ValueError(
000948 |                             f"invalid trace JSON on line {line_number}: {exc}"
000949 |                         ) from exc
000950 |                     validate_json_shape(record)
000951 |                     projected = project_trace_record(record, entry)
000952 |                     if projected is None:
000953 |                         continue
000954 |                     encoded = json.dumps(
000955 |                         projected,
000956 |                         ensure_ascii=False,
000957 |                         sort_keys=True,
000958 |                         separators=(",", ":"),
000959 |                         allow_nan=False,
000960 |                     ).encode("utf-8")
000961 |                     projected_bytes += len(encoded) + (1 if records else 0)
000962 |                     if projected_bytes > MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES:
000963 |                         raise ValueError(
000964 |                             f"trace projection exceeds the "
000965 |                             f"{MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES}-byte output limit"
000966 |                         )
000967 |                     records.append(projected)
000968 |                     if len(records) > MAX_OUTPUT_RECORDS:
000969 |                         raise ValueError(
000970 |                             f"trace exceeds the "
000971 |                             f"{MAX_OUTPUT_RECORDS}-diagnostic output limit"
000972 |                         )
000973 |             return records
000974 |     except (zipfile.BadZipFile, RuntimeError) as exc:
000975 |         raise ValueError(f"invalid or corrupt ZIP entry: {exc}") from exc

000001 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
000002 | """Run a command and atomically publish its validated JSON stdout.
000003 | 
000004 | The output path is resolved beneath the current working directory without
000005 | following symlinked directory components. The command never runs when the
000006 | destination is unsafe.
000007 | """
000008 | 
000009 | from __future__ import annotations

000011 | import argparse
000012 | import json
000013 | import math
000014 | import os
000015 | import secrets
000016 | import selectors
000017 | import signal
000018 | import stat
000019 | import subprocess
000020 | import sys
000021 | import time
000022 | from pathlib import PurePath
000023 | 
000024 | 
000025 | # Keep this publication ceiling aligned with read-playwright-artifact.py.
000026 | MAX_STDOUT_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024
000027 | MAX_COMMAND_SECONDS = 5 * 60
000028 | STREAM_CHUNK_BYTES = 64 * 1024
000029 | TERMINATION_GRACE_SECONDS = 1
000030 | 
000031 | 
000032 | def fail(message: str) -> "NoReturn":
000033 |     raise ValueError(message)
000034 | 
000035 | 
000036 | def relative_parts(raw_path: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
000037 |     path = PurePath(raw_path)
000038 |     if path.is_absolute():
000039 |         fail("output path must be relative to the current working directory")
000040 |     parts = path.parts
000041 |     if not parts or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in parts):
000042 |         fail("output path must not be empty or contain '.' or '..'")
000043 |     if len(parts) < 2:
000044 |         fail("output path must include a report directory")
000045 |     return parts
000046 | 
000047 | 
000048 | def open_output_parent(parts: tuple[str, ...]) -> int:
000049 |     flags = os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY
000050 |     nofollow = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
000051 |     current_fd = os.open(".", flags)
000052 |     try:
000053 |         for component in parts[:-1]:
000054 |             try:
000055 |                 os.mkdir(component, mode=0o700, dir_fd=current_fd)
000056 |             except FileExistsError:
000057 |                 pass
000058 |             next_fd = os.open(component, flags | nofollow, dir_fd=current_fd)
000059 |             os.close(current_fd)
000060 |             current_fd = next_fd
000061 |         return current_fd
000062 |     except BaseException:
000063 |         os.close(current_fd)
000064 |         raise

000067 | def reject_unsafe_destination(parent_fd: int, name: str) -> None:
000068 |     try:
000069 |         metadata = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
000070 |     except FileNotFoundError:
000071 |         return
000072 |     if stat.S_ISLNK(metadata.st_mode):
000073 |         fail("output destination must not be a symlink")
000074 |     if not stat.S_ISREG(metadata.st_mode):
000075 |         fail("output destination must be absent or a regular file")

000077 | 
000078 | def create_temporary(parent_fd: int, destination: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
000079 |     flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL
000080 |     flags |= getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
000081 |     for _ in range(32):
000082 |         temporary = f".{destination}.{os.getpid()}.{secrets.token_hex(8)}.tmp"
000083 |         try:
000084 |             return os.open(temporary, flags, 0o600, dir_fd=parent_fd), temporary
000085 |         except FileExistsError:
000086 |             continue
000087 |     fail("could not allocate a unique temporary report file")

000090 | def reject_duplicate_keys(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
000091 |     value: dict[str, object] = {}
000092 |     for key, item in pairs:
000093 |         if key in value:
000094 |             fail(f"duplicate JSON key: {key}")
000095 |         value[key] = item
000096 |     return value

000098 | 
000099 | def reject_nonfinite_constant(token: str) -> object:
000100 |     fail(f"non-finite JSON number is forbidden: {token}")
000101 | 
000102 | 
000103 | def parse_finite_float(token: str) -> float:
000104 |     value = float(token)
000105 |     if not math.isfinite(value):
000106 |         fail(f"non-finite JSON number is forbidden: {token}")
000107 |     return value

000110 | def validate_json(file_descriptor: int) -> None:
000111 |     os.lseek(file_descriptor, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
000112 |     with os.fdopen(os.dup(file_descriptor), "r", encoding="utf-8") as report:
000113 |         json.load(
000114 |             report,
000115 |             object_pairs_hook=reject_duplicate_keys,
000116 |             parse_constant=reject_nonfinite_constant,
000117 |             parse_float=parse_finite_float,

000121 | def process_group_exists(process_group: int) -> bool:
000122 |     try:
000123 |         os.killpg(process_group, 0)
000124 |     except ProcessLookupError:
000125 |         return False
000126 |     return True

000128 | 
000129 | def terminate_process_group(process: subprocess.Popen[bytes]) -> None:
000130 |     process_group = process.pid
000131 |     try:
000132 |         os.killpg(process_group, signal.SIGTERM)
000133 |     except ProcessLookupError:
000134 |         process.wait()
000135 |         return
000136 | 
000137 |     deadline = time.monotonic() + TERMINATION_GRACE_SECONDS
000138 |     while time.monotonic() < deadline:
000139 |         process.poll()
000140 |         if not process_group_exists(process_group):
000141 |             process.wait()
000142 |             return
000143 |         time.sleep(0.01)
000144 | 
000145 |     try:
000146 |         os.killpg(process_group, signal.SIGKILL)
000147 |     except ProcessLookupError:
000148 |         pass
000149 |     process.wait()

000152 | def capture_stdout(file_descriptor: int, command: list[str]) -> None:
000153 |     process = subprocess.Popen(
000154 |         command,
000155 |         stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
000156 |         start_new_session=True,
000157 |     )
000158 |     deadline = time.monotonic() + MAX_COMMAND_SECONDS
000159 |     cleanup_attempted = False
000160 |     try:
000161 |         if process.stdout is None:
000162 |             fail("could not capture command stdout")
000163 |         with process.stdout, os.fdopen(os.dup(file_descriptor), "wb") as temporary:
000164 |             captured_bytes = 0
000165 |             selector = selectors.DefaultSelector()
000166 |             selector.register(process.stdout, selectors.EVENT_READ)
000167 |             try:
000168 |                 while True:
000169 |                     remaining_seconds = deadline - time.monotonic()
000170 |                     if remaining_seconds <= 0:
000171 |                         cleanup_attempted = True
000172 |                         terminate_process_group(process)
000173 |                         fail(
000174 |                             f"command timed out after {MAX_COMMAND_SECONDS} seconds"
000175 |                         )
000176 |                     if not selector.select(timeout=min(remaining_seconds, 0.1)):
000177 |                         continue
000178 | 
000179 |                     remaining_bytes = MAX_STDOUT_BYTES - captured_bytes
000180 |                     chunk = os.read(
000181 |                         process.stdout.fileno(),
000182 |                         min(STREAM_CHUNK_BYTES, remaining_bytes + 1),
000183 |                     )
000184 |                     if not chunk:
000185 |                         break
000186 |                     captured_bytes += len(chunk)
000187 |                     if captured_bytes > MAX_STDOUT_BYTES:
000188 |                         cleanup_attempted = True
000189 |                         terminate_process_group(process)
000190 |                         fail(
000191 |                             f"command stdout exceeds the {MAX_STDOUT_BYTES}-byte limit"
000192 |                         )
000193 |                     temporary.write(chunk)
000194 |             finally:

000112 | def run_bounded(

000114 |     *,

000131 |     stdout_bytes = 0
000132 |     deadline = time.monotonic() + COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS

000134 |         while selector.get_map():

000155 |                             written = os.write(stdout_fd, view)

000159 |                         chunk[: MAX_API_BYTES - len(captured_stderr)]
000160 |                     )

000162 |         if remaining <= 0:
000163 |             terminate_process_group(process)

000221 | def member_kind(info: zipfile.ZipInfo) -> str:
000222 |     unix_mode = (info.external_attr >> 16) & 0xFFFF
000223 |     mode_kind = stat.S_IFMT(unix_mode)

000226 |         fail(f"symlink ZIP member is forbidden: {info.filename!r}")
000227 |     if mode_kind not in {0, stat.S_IFREG, stat.S_IFDIR}:
000228 |         fail(f"special ZIP member is forbidden: {info.filename!r}")
000229 |     if mode_kind == stat.S_IFDIR and not named_directory:
000230 |         fail(f"ZIP directory mode/name disagreement: {info.filename!r}")
000231 |     if mode_kind == stat.S_IFREG and named_directory:
000232 |         fail(f"ZIP file mode/name disagreement: {info.filename!r}")
000233 |     return "directory" if named_directory or mode_kind == stat.S_IFDIR else "file"

000246 |             os.close(current_fd)

000307 | def rename_noreplace(
000308 |     source_fd: int,
000309 |     source: str,
000310 |     destination_fd: int,
000311 |     destination: str,
000312 | ) -> None:

000318 |             source_fd,
000319 |             source_bytes,
000320 |             destination_fd,
000321 |             destination_bytes,
000322 |             0x00000004,  # RENAME_EXCL
000323 |         )
000324 |     elif hasattr(libc, "renameat2"):
000325 |         result = libc.renameat2(
000326 |             source_fd,
000327 |             source_bytes,
000328 |             destination_fd,
000329 |             destination_bytes,
000330 |             1,  # RENAME_NOREPLACE
000331 |         )
000332 |     else:
000333 |         fail("atomic no-replace directory publication is unavailable")
000334 |     if result != 0:
000335 |         error = ctypes.get_errno()

000046 | def require_secure_descriptor_support() -> tuple[int, int]:
000047 |     directory_flag = getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", None)
000048 |     no_follow_flag = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", None)
000049 |     if (
000050 |         os.name != "posix"
000051 |         or not isinstance(directory_flag, int)
000052 |         or not isinstance(no_follow_flag, int)
000053 |         or os.open not in getattr(os, "supports_dir_fd", set())
000054 |     ):
000055 |         raise ValueError(
000056 |             "secure artifact reading requires POSIX descriptor-relative "
000057 |             "no-follow support (macOS, Linux, or Windows via WSL); "
000058 |             "native Windows is unsupported"
000059 |         )
000060 |     close_on_exec = getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0)
000061 |     return (
000062 |         os.O_RDONLY | directory_flag | no_follow_flag | close_on_exec,
000063 |         os.O_RDONLY
000064 |         | no_follow_flag
000065 |         | getattr(os, "O_NONBLOCK", 0)
000066 |         | close_on_exec,

000071 |     value: dict[str, object] = {}

000074 |             raise ValueError(f"duplicate JSON key: {key}")

000083 | def strict_json_loads(data: bytes | str) -> object:
000084 |     if isinstance(data, bytes):
000085 |         if data.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
000086 |             raise ValueError("JSON BOM is forbidden")
000087 |         try:
000088 |             text = data.decode("utf-8")
000089 |         except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
000090 |             raise ValueError(f"invalid JSON UTF-8: {exc}") from exc
000091 |     else:
000092 |         text = data
000093 |     if text.startswith("\ufeff"):
000094 |         raise ValueError("JSON BOM is forbidden")
000095 |     start = len(text) - len(text.lstrip())
000096 |     if start == len(text):
000097 |         raise ValueError("invalid JSON: input is empty")
000098 |     decoder = json.JSONDecoder(
000099 |         object_pairs_hook=reject_duplicate_keys,
000100 |         parse_constant=reject_nonfinite_number,
000101 |     )
000102 |     try:
000103 |         value, end = decoder.raw_decode(text, start)
000104 |     except (RecursionError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
000105 |         raise ValueError(f"invalid JSON: {exc}") from exc
000106 |     if text[end:].strip():
000107 |         raise ValueError("invalid JSON: trailing data is forbidden")
000108 |     return value

000111 | def open_trusted_directory(path: Path, description: str) -> int:

000158 | @contextmanager
000159 | def open_artifact_descriptor(
000160 |     artifact_root: Path,
000161 |     artifact: Path,
000162 |     max_bytes: int,
000163 | ) -> Iterator[tuple[int, os.stat_result]]:
000164 |     directory_flags, file_flags = require_secure_descriptor_support()
000165 |     absolute_root = Path(os.path.abspath(artifact_root))
000166 |     absolute_artifact = Path(os.path.abspath(artifact))
000167 |     try:
000168 |         lexical_relative = absolute_artifact.relative_to(absolute_root)
000169 |     except ValueError as exc:
000170 |         raise ValueError(f"artifact is outside the artifact root: {artifact}") from exc
000171 |     if not lexical_relative.parts:
000172 |         raise ValueError(f"artifact is not a regular file: {artifact}")
000173 | 
000174 |     root_fd = open_trusted_directory(absolute_root, "artifact root")
000175 |     current_fd = root_fd
000176 |     opened_directory_fds: list[int] = []
000177 |     artifact_fd: int | None = None
000178 |     try:
000179 |         for component in lexical_relative.parts[:-1]:
000180 |             next_fd = os.open(component, directory_flags, dir_fd=current_fd)
000181 |             opened_directory_fds.append(next_fd)
000182 |             current_fd = next_fd
000183 |         artifact_fd = os.open(
000184 |             lexical_relative.parts[-1],
000185 |             file_flags,
000186 |             dir_fd=current_fd,
000187 |         )
000188 |         metadata = os.fstat(artifact_fd)
000189 |         if not stat.S_ISREG(metadata.st_mode):
000190 |             raise ValueError(f"artifact is not a regular file: {artifact}")
000191 |         if metadata.st_size > max_bytes:
000192 |             raise ValueError(
000193 |                 f"artifact exceeds the {max_bytes}-byte limit: {artifact}"
000194 |             )
000195 |         yield artifact_fd, metadata
000196 |     except OSError as exc:
000197 |         raise ValueError(
000198 |             f"unsafe, symlinked, or unreadable artifact path: {artifact}: {exc}"
000199 |         ) from exc
000200 |     finally:
000201 |         if artifact_fd is not None:
000202 |             os.close(artifact_fd)
000203 |         for directory_fd in reversed(opened_directory_fds):
000204 |             os.close(directory_fd)
000205 |         os.close(root_fd)

000208 | def read_artifact(
000209 |     artifact_root: Path,
000210 |     artifact: Path,
000211 |     max_bytes: int,
000212 | ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
000213 |     with open_artifact_descriptor(
000214 |         artifact_root,
000215 |         artifact,
000216 |         max_bytes,
000217 |     ) as (artifact_fd, metadata):
000218 |         chunks: list[bytes] = []
000219 |         remaining = max_bytes + 1
000220 |         while remaining:
000221 |             chunk = os.read(artifact_fd, min(64 * 1024, remaining))
000222 |             if not chunk:
000223 |                 break
000224 |             chunks.append(chunk)
000225 |             remaining -= len(chunk)
000226 |         data = b"".join(chunks)
000227 |         if len(data) > max_bytes:
000228 |             raise ValueError(
000229 |                 f"artifact exceeds the {max_bytes}-byte limit: {artifact}"
000230 |             )
000231 |         require_unchanged_descriptor(artifact_fd, metadata, artifact)
000232 |         if len(data) != metadata.st_size:
000233 |             raise ValueError(f"artifact changed while being read: {artifact}")
000234 |         return metadata.st_size, data

000683 | def run_result_records(report: object) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
000684 |     if not isinstance(report, dict) or not isinstance(report.get("runs"), list):
000685 |         raise ValueError("run-results schema requires a root runs array")

000687 |     for run in report["runs"]:
000688 |         if not isinstance(run, dict):
000689 |             raise ValueError("run-results schema requires run objects")

000691 |         tests = run.get("tests")
000692 |         if not isinstance(spec, dict) or not isinstance(
000693 |             spec.get("relative"), str
000694 |         ) or not isinstance(tests, list):
000695 |             raise ValueError(
000696 |                 "run-results schema requires spec.relative and tests array"
000697 |             )
000698 |         for test in tests:
000699 |             if (
000700 |                 not isinstance(test, dict)
000701 |                 or not isinstance(test.get("title"), list)
000702 |                 or not all(isinstance(part, str) for part in test["title"])
000703 |                 or not isinstance(test.get("state"), str)
000704 |                 or not isinstance(test.get("attempts"), list)
000705 |             ):
000706 |                 raise ValueError(
000707 |                     "run-results schema requires title/state/attempts"
000708 |                 )
000709 |             test_state = test["state"]
000710 |             raw_attempts = test["attempts"]
000711 |             assert isinstance(test_state, str)
000712 |             assert isinstance(raw_attempts, list)
000713 |             if test_state not in CYPRESS_RUN_RESULT_STATES:
000714 |                 raise ValueError(
000715 |                     f"run-results test state is unsupported: {test_state}"
000716 |                 )
000717 |             if not raw_attempts:
000718 |                 raise ValueError(
000719 |                     "run-results tests require at least one attempt"
000720 |                 )
000721 |             attempts: list[dict[str, object]] = []
000722 |             attempt_states: list[str] = []
000723 |             for index, attempt in enumerate(raw_attempts):
000724 |                 if index >= MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_TEST:
000725 |                     raise ValueError(
000726 |                         f"test exceeds the {MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_TEST}-attempt limit"
000727 |                     )
000728 |                 if not isinstance(attempt, dict) or not isinstance(
000729 |                     attempt.get("state"), str
000730 |                 ):
000731 |                     raise ValueError(
000732 |                         "run-results schema requires attempt state strings"
000733 |                     )
000734 |                 attempt_state = attempt["state"]
000735 |                 assert isinstance(attempt_state, str)
000736 |                 if attempt_state not in CYPRESS_RUN_RESULT_STATES:
000737 |                     raise ValueError(
000738 |                         "run-results attempt state is unsupported: "
000739 |                         f"{attempt_state}"
000740 |                     )
000741 |                 attempt_states.append(attempt_state)
000742 |                 attempts.append(
000743 |                     {
000744 |                         "attempt": index,
000745 |                         "state": bounded_string(attempt_state),
000746 |                         "error": error_text(
000747 |                             attempt.get("error")
000748 |                             or attempt.get("displayError")
000749 |                         ),
000750 |                     }
000751 |                 )
000752 |             if attempt_states[-1] != test_state:
000753 |                 raise ValueError(
000754 |                     f"run-results final test state={test_state} contradicts "
000755 |                     f"last attempt state={attempt_states[-1]}"
000756 |                 )
000757 |             records.append(
000758 |                 {

000760 |                     "title": bounded_string(" ".join(test["title"])),
000761 |                     "state": bounded_string(test_state),
000762 |                     "duration": bounded_scalar(test.get("duration")),

000773 | def media_metadata(
000774 |     artifact_root: Path,
000775 |     artifact: Path,

000777 |     suffix = artifact.suffix.lower()
000778 |     if suffix == ".png":
000779 |         kind = "png"
000780 |         max_bytes = MAX_PNG_BYTES
000781 |         expected_magic = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
000782 |     elif suffix == ".mp4":
000783 |         kind = "mp4"
000784 |         max_bytes = MAX_MP4_BYTES
000785 |         expected_magic = None
000786 |     else:
000787 |         raise ValueError("media mode accepts only .png and .mp4 files")
000788 | 
000789 |     snapshot_directory: Path | None = None
000790 |     snapshot_path: Path | None = None
000791 |     try:
000792 |         with open_artifact_descriptor(
000793 |             artifact_root,
000794 |             artifact,
000795 |             max_bytes,
000796 |         ) as (artifact_fd, metadata):
000797 |             header = os.read(artifact_fd, 16)
000798 |             if expected_magic is not None and not header.startswith(
000799 |                 expected_magic
000800 |             ):
000801 |                 raise ValueError("PNG artifact has an invalid signature")
000802 |             if kind == "mp4" and (
000803 |                 len(header) < 12 or header[4:8] != b"ftyp"
000804 |             ):
000805 |                 raise ValueError("MP4 artifact has an invalid ftyp signature")
000806 |             os.lseek(artifact_fd, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
000807 | 
000808 |             snapshot_directory = Path(
000809 |                 tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="e2e-cypress-media-")
000810 |             )
000811 |             os.chmod(snapshot_directory, stat.S_IRWXU)
000812 |             snapshot_path = snapshot_directory / f"artifact.{kind}"
000813 |             snapshot_flags = (
000814 |                 os.O_WRONLY
000815 |                 | os.O_CREAT
000816 |                 | os.O_EXCL
000817 |                 | getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0)
000818 |                 | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
000819 |             )
000820 |             snapshot_fd = os.open(
000821 |                 snapshot_path,
000822 |                 snapshot_flags,
000823 |                 stat.S_IRUSR,
000824 |             )
000825 |             digest = hashlib.sha256()
000826 |             copied = 0
000827 |             try:
000828 |                 while True:
000829 |                     chunk = os.read(artifact_fd, 64 * 1024)
000830 |                     if not chunk:
000831 |                         break
000832 |                     copied += len(chunk)
000833 |                     if copied > max_bytes:
000834 |                         raise ValueError(
000835 |                             f"artifact exceeds the {max_bytes}-byte limit: "
000836 |                             f"{artifact}"
000837 |                         )
000838 |                     digest.update(chunk)
000839 |                     write_all(snapshot_fd, chunk)
000840 |                 require_unchanged_descriptor(
000841 |                     artifact_fd,
000842 |                     metadata,
000843 |                     artifact,
000844 |                 )
000845 |                 if copied != metadata.st_size:
000846 |                     raise ValueError(
000847 |                         f"artifact changed while being read: {artifact}"
000848 |                     )
000849 |                 os.fsync(snapshot_fd)
000850 |                 os.fchmod(snapshot_fd, stat.S_IRUSR)
000851 |                 snapshot_metadata = os.fstat(snapshot_fd)
000852 |                 if (
000853 |                     not stat.S_ISREG(snapshot_metadata.st_mode)
000854 |                     or snapshot_metadata.st_size != copied
000855 |                     or stat.S_IMODE(snapshot_metadata.st_mode)
000856 |                     != stat.S_IRUSR
000857 |                 ):
000858 |                     raise ValueError("media snapshot validation failed")
000859 |             finally:
000860 |                 os.close(snapshot_fd)
000861 | 
000862 |         return {
000863 |             "path": str(snapshot_path),
000864 |             "snapshot_directory": str(snapshot_directory),
000865 |             "kind": kind,
000866 |             "size": copied,
000867 |             "sha256": digest.hexdigest(),
000868 |             "lifecycle": (
000869 |                 "temporary owner-only snapshot; delete snapshot_directory "
000870 |                 "after the viewer closes"
000871 |             ),
000872 |         }
000873 |     except BaseException:
000874 |         remove_failed_snapshot(snapshot_path, snapshot_directory)

000045 | def require_secure_descriptor_support() -> tuple[int, int]:
000046 |     directory_flag = getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", None)
000047 |     no_follow_flag = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", None)

000049 |         os.name != "posix"
000050 |         or not isinstance(directory_flag, int)
000051 |         or not isinstance(no_follow_flag, int)
000052 |         or os.open not in getattr(os, "supports_dir_fd", set())

000054 |         raise ValueError(
000055 |             "secure artifact reading requires POSIX descriptor-relative "
000056 |             "no-follow support (macOS, Linux, or Windows via WSL); "
000057 |             "native Windows is unsupported"
000058 |         )
000059 |     close_on_exec = getattr(os, "O_CLOEXEC", 0)
000060 |     return (
000061 |         os.O_RDONLY | directory_flag | no_follow_flag | close_on_exec,
000062 |         os.O_RDONLY
000063 |         | no_follow_flag
000064 |         | getattr(os, "O_NONBLOCK", 0)
000065 |         | close_on_exec,
